source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Sterling campus publishes 116 MW of IT capacity across three facilities (NVA5, NVA6, NVA7). Assuming 400 kW per rack as a typical density for mixed workloads, this translates to roughly 290 racks. Assuming 8 GPU accelerators per rack at that density, the campus could host approximately 2,320 accelerators if fully deployed for AI training. The operator has published no certifications for this campus.

This campus ranks second by published capacity in Virginia, behind only one other facility. Virginia's 25 facilities with published specifications total 1,603 MW, placing Sterling at 7.2% of the state's declared IT load. Of Virginia's 330 mapped data center facilities, only 25 have disclosed capacity figures, indicating that most infrastructure in the state operates without public specifications.

The technical footprint is 1.18 million square feet. The published IT load implies approximately 98 watts per square foot of technical space, consistent with a broad mix of workload types rather than a pure AI training deployment. Whether this campus matters to AI scaling depends on the actual workload mix and grid availability, neither of which are published.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
